key_insight: MUSE variograms describe glioma MRI heterogeneity by physical distance and direction, with substantial overlap with directional radiomics.
clinical_relevance: This research approach may complement tumor imaging analysis, but it does not establish clinical utility for IDH prediction or treatment decisions.
method: Analyzed postcontrast T1-weighted MRI and enhancing-tumor segmentations from 416 UCSF-PDGM patients.
Compared native 3D MUSE variograms with directional GLCM radiomics in 375 paired cases.
Tested IDH associations using patient-level permutations and evaluated a separate 3D CNN classifier.
evidence_signal: MUSE and half GLCM contrast correlated strongly across 9,371 aligned offsets (r = 0.954); the separate CNN achieved out-of-fold IDH ROC-AUC 0.792 and PR-AUC 0.414.
watch_item: In 364 grade-4 tumors, only 24 were IDH-mutant, and the MUSE–IDH association weakened after directional GLCM adjustment (p = 0.256), limiting evidence of added molecular information.
paper_title: Multiscale Spatial Characterization of Glioma MRI with MUSE and Radiomics
